definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined); national character (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines 'character' in four senses (in a coded character set, in a screen item, in the COBOL character repertoire, in computer storage) and 'coded character set' as "A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set" (taken from ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 drops these entries and takes the terms from its normative reference ISO/IEC 10646 (§2023:2), in the same sense. The rule's 'national character' and 'alphanumeric character' are those senses. 'national character' (§2002:4: "A character in a national character set") is the same notion 2023 uses with its kept 'national character set' entry (§2023:3.125); this compiler's national set is UTF-16 in both editions.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:8.8.1.x (standard arithmetic) and §2002:14.6.4/14.6.6 (SIZE ERROR, arithmetic statements) are not involved: the rule computes no arithmetic result. §2002:15/15.1 differ from 2023 only in 2002's "number of character positions ... is specified in the function definition" and 2023's added type sentence; the rule rests only on the function's category (§2002:15.1 "Unless stated otherwise in the definition of a function, the data item is represented in the national coded character set in effect"), which is the same. §2002:14.5.12.1.2/1.3/14.5.12.2 (fatal and non-fatal processing, incompatible data) differ from 2023, but EC-DATA-CONVERSION is NF in 2002 (§2002:14.5.12.1.5) and is unreachable here: the documented correspondence is the total UTF-16 identity (DOC-A.1-33), shown at --std 2002 by the reader's probes; so no 2002 processing difference is observable.
